categoryMeta.description: Sprint, acceleration, max velocity, speed endurance, 100m/200m/400m development, and race sharpening.

workouts.title: Developing Introduction to Acceleration
workouts.summary: A fundamental acceleration block start session focusing on body lean, leg drive, and foot contact over a short distance.
workouts.riskReason: Explosive standing starts carry minor calf and Achilles strain risks if executed without high-quality neuromuscular activation.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate smoothly to about 90% velocity by the 20-meter mark, then maintain posture to the finish. Keep recoveries generous.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Allow heart rate to spike fully; wait until it returns to a calm aerobic state before launching the next repetition.

warmup.name: General Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 800m easy continuous jog at conversational effort to raise core temperature.

warmup.name: Sprint Mechanics Drills
warmup.description: Dynamic drills: 2 × 20m A-skips, B-skips, High Knees, Butt Kicks, and walking lunges with focus on erect posture.

warmup.name: Progressive Strides
warmup.description: 3 × 50m building strides on a flat straight surface, progressing from 60% up to 85% sprint speed.

mainSet.name: Standing Acceleration Starts
mainSet.description: From a standing 2-point stance, explode forward focusing on pushing the ground away behind you. Sprint 30 meters. Walk back very slowly for recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce repetitions to 4 starts to limit neural fatigue.

mainSet.name: Standing Acceleration Starts (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 30m standing acceleration starts with 150 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase repetitions to 8 starts to build acceleration capacity.

mainSet.name: Standing Acceleration Starts (Extended)
mainSet.description: 8 × 30m standing acceleration starts with 150 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on a low, forward head position for the first 10 meters.
Do not pop straight up on step one; rise gradually like an airplane taking off.
Ensure your recovery is a slow walk to allow ATP stores to fully replenish.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the walk back recovery, which defeats the purpose of central nervous system recovery.
Reaching forward with the foot, which causes braking forces rather than acceleration.
safetyNotes: Ensure the straight surface is completely flat and free of debris.
Keep your calf and Achilles tendon warm by wearing sweatpants until the main set.
Stop immediately if you feel a tight twinge or pull in your hamstring or calf.

shareCard.purposeText: Learn proper body lean and explosive ground drive safely.
shareCard.footerNote: Wear flats or spikes on track or dry turf.

workouts.sourceNote: General sprint training mechanics; consult a sprint coach for block settings.

workouts.title: Intermediate Block Start Acceleration
workouts.summary: A progressive block start acceleration session designed to build muscle power and running economy starting from the blocks.
workouts.riskReason: Maximal speed starts from starting blocks introduce high tendon forces on the Achilles and explosive hamstring contractions.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Execute the start at 95%+ maximal effort. Focus on horizontal projection from the blocks and rapid arm swing.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate spikes extremely high during the 40m burst; wait until it settles completely before starting the next block start.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Block Start Acceleration
mainSet.description: From blocks, explode on the gun or 'go' signal. Run 40 meters at maximal effort. Walk back slowly.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 6 repetitions with 3.5-minute recoveries to limit physical breakdown.

mainSet.name: Block Start Acceleration (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 6 × 40m block starts with 210 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 10 repetitions to challenge starting capacity.

mainSet.name: Block Start Acceleration (Extended)
mainSet.description: 10 × 40m block starts with 180 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Set block pedals at a comfortable angle (usually 45-55 degrees) to allow explosive extension.
On 'set', bring your hips slightly higher than your shoulders and lean your weight forward over your hands.
Drive both arms forcefully—first step arm drives high, rear arm drives back.
commonMistakes: Lifting the head immediately, which halts the horizontal drive phase and forces an early vertical posture.
Stepping out of the blocks (no drive) instead of pushing off both blocks dynamically.
safetyNotes: Do not perform starting block repetitions if you have active Achilles tendon pain.
Ensure your blocks are securely anchored in the track track-pins before stepping in.
Always stretch your calves and Achilles tendons thoroughly during the dynamic warmup phase.

shareCard.purposeText: Build explosive starting block mechanics and lower limb power.
shareCard.footerNote: Spikes are highly recommended for block starts.

workouts.sourceNote: Starting blocks must be adjusted properly to prevent knee injuries.

workouts.title: Advanced Progressive Acceleration
workouts.summary: An advanced session focusing on extending the drive phase and smoothing transitions into maximum velocity.
workouts.riskReason: High-velocity transition phase introduces high knee drive torques and rapid hamstring stretch-shortening cycles.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate for 30 meters, smoothly transition to max velocity over 10 meters, and float the final 10 meters. RPE 9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Allow heart rate to fully recover between reps. Perform deep abdominal breathing in recovery.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Progressive Acceleration Starts
mainSet.description: Sprint 50 meters, focusing on building speed continuously through the first 30m, transitioning to upright sprinting, and floating the final 10m. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 6 repetitions with 4-minute walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: Progressive Acceleration Starts (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 6 × 50m progressive starts with 240 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 10 repetitions with 3.5-minute walking recoveries.

mainSet.name: Progressive Acceleration Starts (Extended)
mainSet.description: 10 × 50m progressive starts with 210 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on pushing down and back, extending your hips fully on each stride.
Think of your drive phase as shifting through gears: gears 1-2 (0-15m), gears 3-4 (15-30m), gear 5 (30-40m).
Maintain a relaxed jaw and shoulders during the transition phase.
commonMistakes: Trying to 'spin' the feet too quickly instead of applying deep force into the track track-surface.
Tensing the shoulders and face during the max speed transition.
safetyNotes: Always wear spikes to ensure optimal traction and prevent slipping during the drive phase.
Ensure your groin and hip flexors are fully stretched and warm before starting.
Always warm up dynamic movement systems to prevent acute hamstring strain or calf pull during the progressive drive phase.

shareCard.purposeText: Master the transition from drive phase to max upright speed.
shareCard.footerNote: Focus on clean transition mechanics.

workouts.sourceNote: Elite sprinters extend their drive phase up to 30-40 meters.

workouts.title: Competitive Sled Starts Acceleration
workouts.summary: A high-resistance sled pull session designed to build horizontal power and explosive start mechanics for competitive sprinters.
workouts.riskReason: High-resistance towing places intense load on the hip flexors, lower back, and calf-Achilles complex.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Sled weight should be 10-12% of your bodyweight. Sprint 40 meters at 100% effort. Focus on pure power.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Fully recover heart rate. Standing recovery with light dynamic stretching between reps.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Resistant Sled Starts
mainSet.description: Pulling a weighted sled (10% of bodyweight), explode from a 3-point start. Sprint 40 meters with maximum effort. Walk back slowly.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce sled weight to 5% of bodyweight and perform 5 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Resistant Sled Starts (Lighter)
mainSet.description: 5 × 40m starts with a 5% bodyweight sled and 240 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 8 repetitions with 12% bodyweight sled pulling.

mainSet.name: Resistant Sled Starts (Heavy)
mainSet.description: 8 × 40m starts with a 12% bodyweight sled and 240 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Do not let the sled overload alter your sprint mechanics. Focus on maintaining a straight line from your head to your rear foot.
Drive your knees hard and high, punching your feet downward and backward into the track track-surface.
A 4-minute recovery is mandatory to preserve maximal force output capabilities.
commonMistakes: Using a sled that is too heavy (greater than 15% bodyweight), which ruins sprint mechanics and slows down leg turnover.
Bending at the waist or looking down, which disrupts hip extension.
safetyNotes: Check sled harness buckles and straps for wear before starting.
Be sure your hip flexors are thoroughly warm to prevent hip pull or calf strain under load.
Execute this session only on a dry, high-traction surface.

shareCard.purposeText: Develop horizontal power and explosive ground-force application.
shareCard.footerNote: Weighted sled and spikes required.

workouts.sourceNote: Resistant sprint training is excellent for horizontal force development.

workouts.title: Intermediate Flying 20m Sprint
workouts.summary: A max-velocity introductory session utilizing a 20-meter acceleration zone and a 20-meter maximal fly zone.
workouts.riskReason: Upright maximum velocity sprinting exposes the hamstrings to extreme high-speed eccentric strain.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate progressively over 20 meters, explode to 100% maximal effort in the 20-meter fly zone, then decelerate smoothly. RPE 10/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Allow heart rate to fully recover to baseline. The goal is neural freshness, not aerobic fatigue.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Flying 20m Sprints
mainSet.description: Use a 20-meter acceleration zone to build up, hit 100% max velocity for a 20-meter timed zone, and decelerate smoothly over 15 meters. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce repetitions to 3 flys with 4.5-minute recoveries to limit eccentric stress.

mainSet.name: Flying 20m Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 3 × Flying 20m sprints with 270 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase repetitions to 5 flys to build speed endurance.

mainSet.name: Flying 20m Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 5 × Flying 20m sprints with 240 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on running 'tall' with high hips and upright posture in the fly zone.
Your foot strike should land directly under your center of mass.
Think of cycling your legs rather than dragging them behind.
commonMistakes: Reaching forward with the foot, causing a heel strike and heavy braking forces.
Decelerating abruptly after the fly zone, which can strain hamstrings.
safetyNotes: Hamstring pulls happen most commonly during max velocity when eccentric load is highest. Ensure your legs are completely warm.
Ensure you have at least 15-20 meters of clear deceleration space beyond the fly zone to prevent hamstring or calf pull.
Perform this workout only when fully rested; do not execute on back-to-back days.

shareCard.purposeText: Build neuromuscular velocity and stride turnover safely.
shareCard.footerNote: Requires cones to mark the acceleration and fly zones.

workouts.sourceNote: Flying sprints are the gold standard for developing maximum speed.

workouts.title: Advanced Flying 30m Speed Play
workouts.summary: An advanced maximum velocity session with a 25-meter acceleration zone and a 30-meter maximal flying zone.
workouts.riskReason: Max velocity over 30 meters taxes the nervous system and places extreme eccentric tension on hamstrings and calves.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate for 25 meters, hold absolute maximum upright speed for 30 meters, then float out. RPE 10/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Let heart rate fully settle. Focus on absolute speed, not a high heart rate.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Flying 30m Sprints
mainSet.description: 25-meter acceleration zone, 30-meter maximal fly zone, 20-meter smooth deceleration. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 5.5-minute recoveries to limit central nervous system fatigue.

mainSet.name: Flying 30m Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × Flying 30m sprints with 330 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 6 repetitions with 5-minute recoveries for highly conditioned sprinters.

mainSet.name: Flying 30m Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 6 × Flying 30m sprints with 300 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on relaxed facial muscles and relaxed shoulders even at absolute peak velocity.
Maintain front-side mechanics: keep your knees high and cycle the feet quickly beneath you.
A 5-minute recovery is necessary for full central nervous system reset.
commonMistakes: Tensing the neck and shoulders in the fly zone, which restricts hip rotation and slows down arm drive.
Shortening recoveries to 'get the workout done,' converting neural speed training into speed endurance.
safetyNotes: Max velocity work has a very-high risk of hamstring pulls and Achilles strains. Ensure your glutes and hamstrings are activated.
Wear high-quality spikes with clean track pins to ensure perfect grip.
Stop immediately if you feel any calf, hamstring, or Achilles discomfort.

shareCard.purposeText: Train the nervous system to coordinate stride mechanics at maximum speed.
shareCard.footerNote: Very-high risk. Spikes and warm track track required.

workouts.sourceNote: CNS recovery takes 5-6 minutes after a maximal speed sprint.

workouts.title: Competitive Flying 40m Speed Peak
workouts.summary: An elite-level maximum velocity session utilizing a 30-meter acceleration zone and a 40-meter maximum speed flying zone.
workouts.riskReason: Maintaining absolute maximum velocity over 40 meters exposes the muscular-tendon structures to maximum shear stresses.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate forcefully for 30 meters, hold peak top-end speed for 40 meters, then float decelerate smoothly. RPE 10/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Deep nose breathing during 6-minute standing/walking recovery. Do not launch until heart rate is fully settled.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Flying 40m Sprints
mainSet.description: 30-meter acceleration zone, 40-meter maximal fly zone, 25-meter smooth deceleration. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 6.5-minute recoveries to limit physical fatigue.

mainSet.name: Flying 40m Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × Flying 40m sprints with 390 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 6 repetitions with 6-minute recoveries for competitive elite sprinters.

mainSet.name: Flying 40m Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 6 × Flying 40m sprints with 360 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on stepping 'down' into the track track-surface rather than 'pushing' behind you at max upright speed.
Keep your torso vertical and hips tucked under your torso.
Use full, expressive arm swings from the shoulder joint; keep elbows bent at 90 degrees.
commonMistakes: Leaning backward at max speed, which drops the hips and leads to hamstring overextension.
Holding breath through the fly zone, causing extreme tension.
safetyNotes: Highly explosive; do not perform this workout if track tracks are wet, damp, or cold to avoid hamstring tear or Achilles strain.
Thorough hamstring, calf, and Achilles activation is critical to avoid acute muscle tears.
If you feel a pull or sharp strain, decelerate immediately.

shareCard.purposeText: Build top-end maximum speed for the second half of the 100m sprint.
shareCard.footerNote: Very-high risk. Spikes and flat track track required.

workouts.sourceNote: Absolute speed work is crucial for breaking 100m personal records.

workouts.title: Elite Flying 10m Velocity Peak
workouts.summary: An elite-reference session designed to record absolute peak maximum velocity using a 30m buildup and a short 10m max velocity fly zone.
workouts.riskReason: Elite top-end sprinting involves maximal eccentric hamstring load, exposing the athlete to significant pull risk.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate progressively for 30 meters, hit absolute maximal speed for 10 meters, and float out smoothly. RPE 10/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Deep rest during the 7-minute recovery. The nervous system must be 100% fresh for each repetition.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Flying 10m Sprints
mainSet.description: 30m acceleration zone, 10m maximal fly zone, 20m deceleration zone. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

easier.description: Reduce to 4 repetitions with 7.5-minute recoveries to limit neurological drain.

mainSet.name: Flying 10m Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × Flying 10m sprints with 450 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 8 repetitions with 7-minute recoveries (Elite reference capacity).

mainSet.name: Flying 10m Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 8 × Flying 10m sprints with 420 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: This session is strictly for tracking maximal stride frequency and hip extension velocity.
Think about 'flying' over the track track—light, rapid, spring-like foot contacts.
Use video analysis to measure hip height and ankle dorsiflexion in the fly zone.
commonMistakes: Pushing hard in the first 10m and fatiguing before reaching the 10m fly zone.
Stiffening the torso or jaw, which slows downs rapid neuromuscular fire.
safetyNotes: Extremely high risk of hamstring pulls, calf tears, and Achilles strain. Athletes must be completely healthy.
Only run on hot, dry days when muscles can maintain maximum temperature.
Keep muscles active during recovery with very light walking.

shareCard.purposeText: Record and train absolute maximum speed and neuromuscular turnover.
shareCard.footerNote: Very-high risk. Spikes and warm track track required.

workouts.sourceNote: Elite sprinters reach top speeds of 11.5 - 12.5 m/s in the flying zone.

workouts.title: Developing 100m Relaxed Speed
workouts.summary: A rhythm session designed to build relaxed sprint coordination and postural control over a full 100-meter distance.
workouts.riskReason: Running a full 100 meters at high speed requires careful pace control to avoid hamstring pull under fatigue.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run 100 meters at a controlled, smooth sprint (around 85% velocity, RPE 8). Focus on rhythm and dynamic arm drive.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate stable in high anaerobic zone; walk recovery slowly until breathing returns to a steady rhythm.

warmup.name: General Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 800m easy continuous jog at conversational effort to raise core temperature.

warmup.name: Sprint Mechanics Drills
warmup.description: Dynamic drills: 2 × 20m A-skips, B-skips, High Knees, Butt Kicks, and walking lunges with focus on erect posture.

warmup.name: Progressive Strides
warmup.description: 3 × 50m building strides on a flat straight surface, progressing from 60% up to 85% sprint speed.

mainSet.name: Relaxed 100m Sprints
mainSet.description: Sprint 100 meters at 85% effort, focusing on staying relaxed in the face and shoulders. Walk back slowly for recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

mainSet.name: Relaxed 100m Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 6 × 100m sprints with 210 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 10 repetitions to challenge posture stability.

mainSet.name: Relaxed 100m Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 10 × 100m sprints with 180 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on shoulder carriage: keep shoulders down and back, not hunched.
Maintain high knees and avoid 'shuffling' your stride.
Imagine your head is being pulled up by a string, keeping your torso tall.
commonMistakes: Clenching fists and neck muscles, which slows down shoulder rotation.
Overstriding in the final 20 meters, which leads to heavy heel-strikes and deceleration.
safetyNotes: Warm up thoroughly before beginning the 100m repetitions to avoid acute hamstring pull or calf pull.
Always stretch calves, hamstrings, and hip flexors dynamically.
Be sure the surface is dry and flat to prevent ankle twists.

shareCard.purposeText: Develop smooth rhythm and postural control over a full 100m distance.
shareCard.footerNote: Can be run on grass or turf to reduce impact.

workouts.sourceNote: Relaxed sprinting is key to unlocking speed; tension is the enemy.

workouts.title: Intermediate 100m Progressive Build-ups
workouts.summary: A multi-pace structured speed workout designed to build acceleration and top-end float transitions safely.
workouts.riskReason: Transitioning through different sprint intensities introduces eccentric load changes on the hamstrings.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: First 30m accelerate dynamically, middle 40m float/maintain, final 30m re-accelerate to max speed. RPE 9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Wait until breathing settles fully before each repetition. Recoveries are walking.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: 100m Build-Up Sprints
mainSet.description: Sprint 100 meters: Accelerate for 30m, float/glide for 40m, then re-accelerate to max speed for the final 30m. Walk back recovery.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

mainSet.name: 100m Build-Up Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 100m build-ups with 270 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 8 repetitions to develop higher endurance.

mainSet.name: 100m Build-Up Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 8 × 100m build-ups with 240 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on a smooth transition into the 'float' phase; do not drop speed, just reduce the effort needed to maintain it.
Keep your hips high and step down cleanly on the track track-surface.
During the final 30m re-acceleration, focus on rapid arm drive to prompt leg turnover.
commonMistakes: Coasting too slow during the float phase, losing all momentum.
Overstriding or straining during the re-acceleration phase, which increases injury risk.
safetyNotes: A thorough dynamic warmup is essential to handle the shifts in muscle contraction velocities and avoid hamstring or calf strain.
Always stretch calves, hamstrings, and Achilles tendons beforehand.
Stop immediately if you feel a sudden tightness in your legs.

shareCard.purposeText: Master velocity transition and build high-speed efficiency.
shareCard.footerNote: Requires full concentration on pacing phases.

workouts.sourceNote: Buildup runs teach horizontal energy conservation.

workouts.title: Advanced 100m Curve-to-Straight
workouts.summary: A technical curve-running session designed to master acceleration on the bend and transition into maximum upright speed on the straightaway.
workouts.riskReason: Centrifugal forces on the curve place asymmetric strains on the knees, ankles, and inner groin muscles.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Accelerate hard off the curve (first 50 meters), smoothly square up on the straight, and float the final 50 meters. RPE 9/10.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Deep walking recoveries. Maintain full neural focus. Wait until breathing is completely relaxed.

warmup.name: Neuromuscular Warmup Jog
warmup.description: 1000m progressive easy jog, starting very slow and ending with a light clip to prepare muscle spindles.

warmup.name: Dynamic Mobilization & Sprint Drills
warmup.description: Leg swings (10 per leg), arm swings, followed by 2 × 30m A-Skips, B-Skips, Fast-Leg drills, and Boundings with focus on high hip posture and front-side mechanics.

warmup.name: Acceleration Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 50m progressive strides (65%, 75%, 85%, 92% effort) to prep hamstrings and Achilles for maximal explosive load.

mainSet.name: Curve-to-Straight Sprints
mainSet.description: Start at the 200m mark curve. Sprint 100 meters: Accelerate around the curve, and float upright down the straightaway. Walk back slowly.

cooldown.name: Active Recovery Walk
cooldown.description: 400m slow walking to flush metabolites and lower heart rate gradually.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching
cooldown.description: 10 mins of gentle static stretching focusing on the hamstrings, calf muscles, hip flexors, and Achilles tendon. Do not bounce.

mainSet.name: Curve-to-Straight Sprints (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 4 × 100m curve sprints with 330 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 8 repetitions to develop curves endurance.

mainSet.name: Curve-to-Straight Sprints (Extended)
mainSet.description: 8 × 100m curve sprints with 300 seconds walking recovery.

coachingNotes: Lean into the curve from your ankles, not your waist.
Drive your right arm across your torso slightly to help counteract centrifugal forces.
